# Build a Multilingual Voice AI Companion on Reachy Mini

This community recipe shows how to embed Agora Conversational AI into a Pollen Robotics Reachy Mini. The finished application listens through a browser microphone, transcribes English, Hindi, Tamil, Hinglish, and Tamil-English, replies with a multilingual voice, routes that voice to Reachy's speaker, and performs safe gestures, expressions, and dances.

The current implementation is designed and validated specifically for Reachy Mini. It combines Agora's real-time conversational layer with Pollen Robotics' robot media, movement APIs, Control app catalogs, and Hugging Face-based app distribution. It is a community integration and does not imply an official partnership or endorsement unless the respective teams say so.

## Why This Recipe Matters

Reachy Mini already gives developers an expressive physical platform. Agora Conversational AI adds the real-time voice layer needed to turn that platform into a multilingual companion people can speak with naturally.

For the Pollen Robotics community, this recipe provides a complete example instead of isolated voice and motion experiments: authentication, live audio, transcription, synthesized speech, safe action dispatch, dances, expressions, deployment, and public-demo cost controls all work together.

For the Agora community, it demonstrates conversational AI embodied in real hardware. The value is not a scripted chatbot beside a robot; the conversation, speaker output, transcript, agent state, and physical response share one coordinated experience.

## What You Will Build

By the end of the recipe, you will have:

- a low-latency voice conversation powered by Agora Conversational AI;
- Agora ARES multilingual speech recognition for English, Hindi, and Tamil;
- natural language and code-switching responses from a managed OpenAI model;
- Murf Anisha speech routed to Reachy Mini's speaker;
- live transcripts, agent state, provider latency, and a copyable agent ID;
- 11 bounded utility gestures, 34 dances, and 81 expressions;
- spoken movement commands derived only from finalized user transcripts;
- a local USB development mode and a hosted Reachy Discover Apps mode;
- optional per-account public-demo limits backed by Upstash Redis.

## Try the Finished Experience

Open the [hosted Reachy Companion Space](https://huggingface.co/spaces/rrsa12/agora-reachy-voice-ai-companion).

The hosted experience requires:

- a Hugging Face account;
- a Reachy Mini associated with that account and online in Reachy Mini Control;
- microphone permission in the browser;
- an available public-demo allowance.

The final experience requires Reachy Mini. Developers can use `/?agoraOnly=1` as a diagnostic mode to verify Agora credentials and conversation behavior through a computer microphone and speaker before connecting the robot, but it is not the intended end-user experience.

## Two Ways to Adopt It

### Install and try the community app

Reachy Mini owners can open the public Hugging Face Space from Reachy Mini Control, connect a robot associated with their Hugging Face account, and try the hosted companion without first cloning the code. The public instance includes a limited daily allowance so community members can evaluate the interaction safely.

### Deploy an owned copy

Developers, educators, labs, and event teams can clone the Space repository, connect their own Agora project and Murf account, customize the companion, and deploy a separate Docker Space. This is the recommended path for continued use because each adopter owns their provider limits, prompt, access policy, and operating costs.

## Architecture

![Agora Reachy Voice AI Companion architecture](https://huggingface.co/spaces/rrsa12/agora-reachy-voice-ai-companion/resolve/main/system-architecture.svg)

The application has four cooperating layers:

```text
User and Reachy Mini
  │
  │ microphone audio / synthesized speech / safe movement
  ▼
Next.js browser application
  ├─ Agora RTC: publishes the user microphone and subscribes to agent audio
  ├─ Agora RTM: receives transcripts, agent state, errors, and latency metrics
  ├─ completed-transcript matcher: selects one allow-listed robot action
  └─ Reachy SDK or local daemon: plays the selected movement
  │
  ▼
Next.js server routes
  ├─ issue RTC + RTM tokens
  ├─ start and stop managed Agora agents
  ├─ keep Agora and Murf credentials server-side
  └─ enforce the optional hosted usage allowance
  │
  ▼
Agora Conversational AI
  └─ ARES ASR → managed OpenAI LLM → Murf TTS
```

### Conversation path

1. The browser requests an RTC-and-RTM-capable Agora token.
2. The server starts one managed conversational agent for the browser user.
3. The browser publishes the selected microphone through Agora RTC.
4. Agora ARES recognizes the configured languages without replacing the agent.
5. The managed OpenAI model mirrors the language or language mixture from the latest turn.
6. Murf synthesizes the response with Anisha, and the subscribed audio track is routed to Reachy's speaker.
7. Agora RTM delivers finalized transcripts, agent state, metrics, and errors to the UI.

### Robot-action path

Agora's managed tools execute in the cloud and cannot safely call a USB daemon on `localhost`. This application therefore uses a local action bridge:

1. Wait for a finalized local-user transcript.
2. Match only an explicit allow-listed gesture, dance, or expression command.
3. Pause agent playback and temporarily mute the published microphone.
4. Play the movement through the local daemon or hosted Reachy SDK.
5. Wait for actual movement completion, then restore the previous microphone state.

This prevents music from a dance from being recognized as a new user turn, avoids overlapping long movements, and never exposes the local robot daemon through a public tunnel.

## Technology Stack

| Layer | Technology |
| --- | --- |
| Web application | Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript |
| Live audio | Agora RTC through `agora-rtc-react` |
| Transcripts and agent events | Agora RTM and `agora-agent-client-toolkit` |
| Agent lifecycle | `agora-agents` server SDK |
| Speech recognition | Agora ARES, with Deepgram Nova-3 fallback |
| Language model | Managed OpenAI `gpt-4o-mini` |
| Speech synthesis | Murf Falcon with Anisha |
| Robot integration | Reachy Mini browser SDK and local daemon API |
| Hosted demo | Docker Hugging Face Space |
| Optional demo metering | Upstash Redis REST API |

## Choose a Setup Path

| Goal | Start with |
| --- | --- |
| Diagnose Agora before connecting Reachy | `/?agoraOnly=1` |
| Build with a USB Reachy Mini Lite | `/?lite=1` |
| Use Reachy Mini Discover Apps | Docker Hugging Face Space |

The Agora-only path is the quickest diagnostic for credentials and conversation behavior. Complete the recipe with Reachy Mini after the voice pipeline works independently.

## Prerequisites

### Required for every setup

- Node.js 22 or newer;
- `pnpm`;
- an Agora project with Conversational AI enabled;
- the Agora App ID and App Certificate;
- a Murf API account and API key.

### Required for Reachy hardware

- an assembled Reachy Mini;
- Reachy Mini Control installed and running;
- a USB connection for Lite mode, or a Hugging Face-linked robot for hosted mode;
- motors enabled and the robot awake before starting a conversation.

### Required for the hosted public demo

- a Docker-capable Hugging Face Space;
- Hugging Face OAuth enabled by the Space metadata;
- Upstash Redis REST credentials, unless hosted quota enforcement is explicitly disabled.

## 1. Install the Project

Clone the public source repository or the Hugging Face Space repository, then install dependencies:

```bash
git clone https://huggingface.co/spaces/rrsa12/agora-reachy-voice-ai-companion
cd agora-reachy-voice-ai-companion
pnpm install
```

If you already have the Agora CLI, bind your project and generate the local environment file:

```bash
agora login
agora project use <your-project>
agora project env write .env.local
```

Alternatively, copy the tracked template:

```bash
cp env.local.example .env.local
```

Never commit `.env.local`.

## 2. Configure the Voice Pipeline

Add these values to `.env.local`:

```bash
NEXT_PUBLIC_AGORA_APP_ID=<your-agora-app-id>
NEXT_AGORA_APP_CERTIFICATE=<your-agora-app-certificate>
NEXT_MURF_API_KEY=<your-murf-api-key>

# Defaults shown explicitly
NEXT_ASR_PROVIDER=ares
NEXT_MURF_VOICE_ID=en-IN-anisha
NEXT_MURF_VOICE_GENDER=female
```

The default agent pipeline is:

```text
Agora ARES ASR: en-IN,hi-IN,ta-IN
        ↓
Managed OpenAI: gpt-4o-mini
        ↓
Murf Falcon TTS: en-IN-anisha
```

The Murf key and Agora App Certificate are server-only. Do not prefix either name with `NEXT_PUBLIC_`.

### Why ARES uses a comma-separated language value

Agora ARES accepts multiple BCP-47 language tags in one `asr.language` string:

```text
en-IN,hi-IN,ta-IN
```

The current `agora-agents` high-level turn-detection field accepts one locale, so the application keeps `en-IN` there for VAD validation and updates the serialized ARES request with all three languages. Do not replace the value with an array.

### Deepgram fallback

To test the managed Deepgram Nova-3 multilingual fallback:

```bash
NEXT_ASR_PROVIDER=deepgram
```

Restart or redeploy after changing the provider. No separate Deepgram key is required for the managed fallback used here.

## 3. Verify the Environment

Run the built-in checks before opening a conversation:

```bash
pnpm run doctor
pnpm run verify
```

The verification chain covers linting, TypeScript, API contracts, and a production build.

## 4. Test the Conversation Without Reachy

Start the development server:

```bash
pnpm run dev
```

Open:

```text
http://localhost:3000/?agoraOnly=1
```

Click **Wake Up & Talk**, allow microphone access, and verify:

1. The greeting plays.
2. Your words appear in the transcript.
3. The agent ID appears in the left troubleshooting panel.
4. The provider chips show ARES, OpenAI, and Murf.
5. English, Hindi, Tamil, and natural code-switching produce matching replies.

Resolve voice-pipeline problems here before introducing the robot audio path.

## 5. Connect Reachy Mini over USB

1. Assemble Reachy Mini and connect it to the Mac over USB.
2. Open Reachy Mini Control.
3. Enable the motors and wake the robot.
4. Keep Reachy Mini Control running.
5. Open:

```text
http://localhost:3000/?lite=1
```

The validated default uses the MacBook microphone and Reachy's USB speaker. This avoids depending on a damaged or unavailable physical robot microphone.

To select the robot microphone explicitly after testing the hardware:

```text
http://localhost:3000/?lite=1&mic=reachy
```

When **Wake Up & Talk** is pressed, the local route:

1. enables the motors;
2. plays Reachy's canonical wake-up trajectory;
3. releases daemon media ownership;
4. lets the browser publish the selected microphone and route agent audio to the robot speaker.

Always end the conversation normally. Cleanup centers the robot, cancels active motion, and returns media ownership to the daemon.

## 6. Test Gestures, Dances, and Expressions

Try short utility commands first:

- “Nod.”
- “Tilt your head.”
- “Look left.”
- “Wiggle your antennas.”
- “Take a bow.”

Then test one recorded performance:

- “Do a pendulum swing.”
- “Do side peekaboo.”
- “Look cheerful.”
- “Act curious.”

The UI exposes the complete searchable catalog and a Stop control. New movements remain blocked until the active daemon move actually finishes.

The voice agent acknowledges a physical command briefly but does not narrate or pretend the movement succeeded. The local hardware path is the source of truth.

## 7. Understand the Multilingual Behavior

The browser does not present a language selector. One agent remains active while the user changes language.

- English input receives natural Indian English.
- Hindi input receives Hindi in Devanagari.
- Tamil input receives Tamil in Tamil script.
- Hinglish receives a natural Hindi-English mixture.
- Tamil-English receives a natural Tamil-English mixture.

The LLM prompt mirrors the most recent turn automatically. ASR can revise its provisional language or script, so user partial transcripts are hidden until finalization.

Within-utterance code-switching remains provider best-effort. Always test the accents and acoustic conditions expected in your deployment.

## 8. Customize the Companion

### Change the personality and guardrails

Edit `REACHY_COMPANION_PROMPT` in:

```text
app/api/invite-agent/route.ts
```

Keep the instructions short enough for a spoken interaction. The sample includes family-friendly boundaries, language mirroring, honest capability statements, and silent physical-action behavior.

### Change the greeting

Edit:

```text
lib/conversation-languages.ts
```

### Change the Murf voice

Set both the voice ID and its grammatical identity:

```bash
NEXT_MURF_VOICE_ID=<falcon-compatible-voice-id>
NEXT_MURF_VOICE_GENDER=female
```

Use `male` when selecting a male voice. The prompt uses this value to keep English pronouns and Hindi/Tamil self-reference consistent.

### Add a safe utility gesture

Add bounded movement metadata and sequences in:

```text
lib/reachy-actions.ts
```

Add spoken phrases and catalog routing in:

```text
lib/reachy-performances.ts
```

Never dispatch arbitrary motor coordinates from an LLM response. Preserve validation, serialization, completion tracking, cancellation, and neutral return.

## 9. Deploy as a Docker Hugging Face Space

The server routes require private credentials, so deploy this variant as a Docker Space rather than a static Space.

Create the Space with Docker SDK and configure these variables:

```text
AGORA_APP_ID
NEXT_MURF_VOICE_ID=en-IN-anisha
NEXT_MURF_VOICE_GENDER=female
```

Configure these as secrets:

```text
NEXT_AGORA_APP_CERTIFICATE
NEXT_MURF_API_KEY
```

Hugging Face supplies `OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`, `SPACE_ID`, `SPACE_HOST`, and `SPACE_SIGNING_SECRET` at runtime. Do not add a Hugging Face access token to a public environment variable.

The included Dockerfile builds the standalone Next.js server and listens on `0.0.0.0:7860`.

### Enable the five-minute public-demo allowance

Add these Upstash values as Space secrets:

```text
UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL
UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN
```

Hosted Spaces enforce quota by default. The sample allows five elapsed conversation minutes per authenticated Hugging Face account per UTC day, one active conversation at a time.

Optional controls:

```bash
DAILY_USAGE_LIMIT_SECONDS=300
NEXT_PUBLIC_EXTENDED_ACCESS_URL=<public-contact-or-discussion-url>
```

For a private deployment where you intentionally do not want the shared quota store:

```bash
USAGE_QUOTA_MODE=disabled
```

Do not disable it on a public demo that uses your Agora and Murf credentials unless another cost-control system is in place.

### Qualify for Reachy Discover Apps

Keep the following in the public Space repository:

- the exact `reachy_mini_js_app` tag in the README metadata;
- `public/icon.svg`;
- Docker Space metadata and port `7860`;
- a public Space after private testing succeeds.

Catalog publication is moderated and can take time after the Space becomes public.

## 10. Production and Security Notes

- Keep the Agora App Certificate and every provider key on the server.
- Generate RTC and RTM access with `RtcTokenBuilder.buildTokenWithRtm`; an RTC-only token breaks transcript events.
- Treat browser inputs, RTM payloads, and transcript text as untrusted.
- Use a signed, HttpOnly, Secure, partitioned session for hosted iframe API calls.
- Bind public usage to an authenticated account identity, not only an IP address.
- Never expose the Reachy USB daemon through an unauthenticated tunnel.
- Keep motion bounded and allow-listed, and provide cancellation.
- Run `pnpm run verify` before every deployment.

The included quota is a public-demo cost guard, not a billing or entitlement system. Commercial deployments should add their own user model, observability, durable request limits, provider budgets, and incident controls.

## Troubleshooting

### The agent does not start

- Run `pnpm run doctor`.
- Confirm the Agora App ID and Certificate belong to the same enabled project.
- Confirm the Murf key is valid.
- Inspect the `/api/invite-agent` response and the active agent ID panel.

### No user transcript appears

- Confirm microphone permission and input level.
- Test `/?agoraOnly=1` first.
- Keep token generation on `buildTokenWithRtm`.
- Verify RTM login and subscription errors in the connection panel.

### Reachy does not appear in the hosted picker

- Keep Reachy Mini Control running.
- Confirm the robot and browser use the same Hugging Face account.
- If a local Lite session ended abnormally, restore daemon media ownership and refresh the hosted app.

### Reachy speaks through the Mac instead of the robot

- Verify the Reachy USB output exists in macOS audio devices.
- Confirm the Lite preparation route released daemon media.
- Test the Agora-only path separately from robot speaker routing.

### An action is recognized but does not move

- Try the same action from the UI button.
- Confirm motors are enabled.
- Check whether another recorded movement is still active.
- Verify the configured dance and expression datasets are available to the daemon.

### The public demo allowance is unavailable

- Confirm both Upstash REST secrets exist in the Space.
- Paste the raw values without surrounding quotes when possible.
- Check the Space logs for an Upstash authorization or URL error.

## Verification Checklist

Before sharing an adaptation, verify:

- [ ] Agora-only conversation starts and stops cleanly.
- [ ] English, Hindi, and Tamil final transcripts appear.
- [ ] The reply follows the user's latest language.
- [ ] Murf audio reaches the expected speaker.
- [ ] The active agent ID is visible and copyable.
- [ ] Reachy wakes into a neutral, centered pose.
- [ ] Utility actions complete and return safely.
- [ ] A recorded dance can be stopped.
- [ ] The microphone is quiet while music or movement runs.
- [ ] Ending restores daemon media and robot availability.
- [ ] No certificates, API keys, access tokens, or local `.env` files are public.
- [ ] Hosted quota expiry stops the agent and updates the daily allowance.

## Key Files

| Purpose | File |
| --- | --- |
| Agent prompt and STT/LLM/TTS pipeline | `app/api/invite-agent/route.ts` |
| RTC + RTM token generation | `app/api/generate-agora-token/route.ts` |
| Agent shutdown | `app/api/stop-conversation/route.ts` |
| Local Reachy daemon bridge | `app/api/reachy-lite/route.ts` |
| Session bootstrap | `components/LandingPage.tsx` |
| RTC/RTM and audio routing | `components/ConversationComponent.tsx` |
| Hardware action controls | `components/ReachyActionControls.tsx` |
| Multilingual ARES adapter | `lib/asr-provider.ts` |
| Movement catalogs and phrase matching | `lib/reachy-performances.ts` |
| Hosted Reachy playback | `lib/reachy-browser-performance.ts` |
| Signed hosted API session | `lib/api-security.ts` |
| Durable public-demo allowance | `lib/usage-quota.ts` |

## Where to Go Next

Once the baseline is working, consider:

- adding vision or proximity context without changing the voice transport;
- defining structured Reachy command schemas instead of phrase matching;
- adding user profiles and opt-in memory with clear retention controls;
- moving from a shared public demo to per-developer Agora credentials;
- evaluating ASR accuracy with a multilingual test set from your real environment;
- adding structured telemetry for conversation latency, Reachy movement completion, and provider failures;
- publishing new Reachy expressions and companion personalities as community extensions.

The central pattern stays the same: Agora provides the real-time conversational layer, while the Reachy integration turns validated conversational intent into safe, expressive behavior on a Pollen Robotics device.

## Share It With the Community

When presenting the project, use accurate, reproducible claims:

- **What it is:** a community-built multilingual Agora Conversational AI companion for Pollen Robotics Reachy Mini.
- **What people can try:** a live conversation, automatic language following, transcripts, gestures, dances, and expressions.
- **What adopters receive:** public source, a Docker deployment, a hardware setup path, verification commands, and clearly separated provider credentials.
- **What it is not:** an official Pollen Robotics or Agora product announcement, a claim of autonomous consciousness, or a universal robot integration.

The strongest demonstration is short: show Reachy waking, hold one English exchange, switch naturally to Hindi or Tamil, request one bounded expression or dance, and end the session cleanly. Include the transcript and pipeline chips in frame so viewers can see that the interaction is powered by Agora Conversational AI rather than prerecorded audio.
